coverage_note: Four guidelines spanning the screening/diagnosis/surveillance/repair pathway from three regions (USPSTF 2019 US, NICE NG156 UK, ESVS 2024 Europe, SVS 2018 US). ESVS 2024 is the most recent and most detailed and supplies the majority of indexed chunks.

low_value_material_excluded_from_index.policy: Labelled, retained in chunks.json for traceability, and filtered out of the index only.

duplicates.interpretation: Measured on the frozen normalisation, the index contains NO exactly duplicated chunk text. Overlapping chunks share a 40-token tail by design, so near-duplicates exist by construction, but no chunk is a full copy of another. Deduplication is therefore not needed.

recommendation_completeness.interpretation: Recommendation IDs are attached post hoc by excerpt/ID matching against page-buffer chunks; units split by pagination lose the match. Atomic chunking (Experiment 12) raises attachment substantially.

section_metadata.known_defect: Inherited titles import artifacts (running headers, table captions). Experiment 3 measured this and also established that section_title is never embedded, so it is a provenance/display issue, not a retrieval one.

sources: USPSTF_2019: I statement / D recommendation depending on smoking history
NICE_NG156 1.1.3 (p7): consider aortic ultrasound for women 70+ with risk factors
SVS_2018 (p15): one-time screening in men OR women 65-75 with tobacco use
known_conflicting_recommendations.nature: Genuine guideline disagreement. A retrieval system must surface all three, not pick one.

verdict_on_coverage: No evidence of a coverage gap was found. Every question in all three frozen sets has at least one indexed chunk that satisfies the frozen relevance rule (see question_audit.json, field relevant_chunks_available_in_index). Adding documents is therefore NOT recommended: the measured ceiling is retrieval, not corpus content.
